clue.text: Selectivity a start on it in gallery

indicators.note: in puts the start letter within the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is the London art gallery
'it' points back at the word Selectivity, whose start is S

explanation.surface: A connoisseur's discernment is put on show at an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers to the clue's first word, so 'a start on it' is that word's first letter, S, which goes 'in' TATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Good taste is discernment, a capacity for choosing well among things.

clue.text: Perhaps whisky and beer hits end in one's complete blackout

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirit, whisky being an example
ale is a kind of beer
clips are blows or hits

indicators.note: end in means the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Drinking spirits and beer leaves one completely blacked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end in' takes E from one's. The surface suggests passing out drunk; the definition is the sun wholly hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: A total eclipse is when the sun is entirely blotted out, a complete blackout of its light.

clue.text: Power displayed by second eleven, possibly

parts.note: an eleven is a team, as in cricket or football

explanation.surface: Strength shown by a reserve side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second eleven' looks like a reserve side, but the words split: S and TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam is motive power, as in steam engines.

clue.text: Run a piece that's blasted follower of luxury

indicators.note: something blasted is blown apart, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier runs at a gun that has been fired, despite a love of comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's blasted' rearranges RUN A PIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicurean is devoted to sensual pleasure and fine food.

clue.text: Primate hard at work, holding pencil given by a bishop

indicators.note: holding means the first piece wraps round the others

parts.note: someone hard at work is busy
HB is the standard pencil grade, hard-black
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An industrious person clutches a pencil a bishop has handed over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard at work' reads as describing the primate, but it is one piece; 'holding' wraps it round the pencil grade, A and the chess bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: The bushbaby, or galago, is a small nocturnal African primate.

clue.text: Arrived unexpectedly, being unhappy with pub, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means these words are said aloud to give a word sounding the same

parts.note: unhappy means blue, and a pub is an inn

explanation.surface: Someone turned up suddenly, gloomy about the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: BLUE INN said aloud sounds like BLEW IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow in is an informal idiom for to turn up casually or unexpectedly.

clue.text: Almost defenceless, caught by what cobra may do in reptile house?

indicators.note: caught by means the next piece is held within the spitting word

parts.note: a spitting cobra spits venom

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: naked means unprotected or defenceless

explanation.surface: A nearly defenceless person is struck by a cobra at a zoo's reptile house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts NAKED to NAKE, which is 'caught by' SPIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake pit is an enclosure full of snakes, hence a reptile house, with a question mark for the loose fit.

clue.text: Black, with nothing added — man taking a tea

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
O is zero, nothing
he is a man

explanation.surface: Black, with no milk or sugar — a man is having a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black, with nothing added' looks like how tea is taken, but each word gives a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohea is a type of black China tea.

clue.text: Good liver from Perigord — one appreciating it?

definitions.meaning: the French words, as from the Perigord region of France, translate literally as good liver
someone who appreciates fine food and the good life

explanation.surface: Foie gras from the Perigord, enjoyed by a gourmet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good liver from Perigord' suggests the region's famous goose liver; read as French it is literally 'good liver', a person who lives well.
explanation.definitionFit: A bon viveur is someone who enjoys good food and drink, literally a good liver.

clue.text: Clock, say, one associates with Wells?

definitions.text: Clock, say, one associates with Wells?

parts.words: Clock, say, one associates with Wells?
parts.note: a clock is a device that measures time, and the author H. G. Wells wrote a famous novel about a device for travelling through it

explanation.surface: A timepiece that some people link with the cathedral city of Wells.
explanation.walkthrough: Wells seems to be the Somerset city, but it is the novelist H. G. Wells, whose 1895 story features a time-travelling device.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock could jokingly be called a device for time, and Wells's novel bears that title.

clue.text: I note detectives and more not out of place here

definitions.text: I note detectives and more not out of place here

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British detectives

indicators.note: out of place means the letters are disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone observes detectives and others crowding into an unsuitable spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of place' rearranges MORE NOT to ENTROOM. The whole clue describes the police room where detectives gather.
explanation.definitionFit: An incident room is a police base set up to run an investigation, where detectives gather.

clue.text: Left one timid character going round in big car

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: going round means the creature's letters enclose the next word

parts.note: a timid person is called a mouse
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shy person is left alone, driving round in a large car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timid character' seems to describe a person; it is the rodent, and 'going round' makes it enclose the little word that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A limousine is a large luxurious chauffeur-driven car.

clue.text: Strange article about golfer's position

indicators.note: about means the article sits around the golfing term

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a golf ball's lie is the position where it comes to rest

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece concerns where a golfer stands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' suggests a newspaper piece but is the grammatical article; 'about' makes it surround the golfing term.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien as an adjective means foreign or unfamiliar.

clue.text: Distinguishing feature long seen in Court?

indicators.note: seen in means the yearning word is placed inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: A mark of distinction that has been observed in a law court for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective of time but is the verb, giving ACHE, which is 'seen in' CT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cachet is a distinctive mark or quality conferring prestige.

clue.text: Drink supplier caught with free tea I brewed

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: brewed suggests something stewed and mixed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is caught with free tea that they made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink supplier' sounds like a person serving drinks, but it is a coffee pot; 'brewed' signals the rearrangement of the three words after the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafetiere is a plunger pot that supplies coffee.

clue.text: Scandalous diaries about Liberal prime minister

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters wrap round the party abbreviation
scandalous suggests something disreputable and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shocking diaries about a member of the Liberal party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scandalous' rearranges DIARIES to DISRAEI, and 'about' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian Conservative prime minister of Britain.

clue.text: Church pressed hard in list of duties for cathedral

indicators.note: in means the combined piece goes inside the list

parts.note: a roster is a list of duties

indicators.note: pressed means the church abbreviation squeezes the next letter inside it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church squeezed hard into the duty rota.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: 'pressed' squeezes the hard abbreviation into the Church of England's, and 'in' puts that inside the list of duties.
explanation.definitionFit: Rochester in Kent has an ancient cathedral, so it is a cathedral city.

clue.text: A light touch, over a short distance if necessary

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: a tap is a light touch
an inch is a short distance

explanation.surface: Something touched gently across a small gap, if need be.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts A TAP above INCH.
explanation.definitionFit: At a pinch is an idiom meaning in an emergency, if really necessary.

clue.text: There's no end to what Blake innocently palmed

definitions.text: There's no end to what Blake innocently palmed

parts.words: There's no end to what Blake innocently palmed
parts.note: in Blake's Auguries of Innocence the reader holds something endless in the palm of the hand

explanation.surface: A remark on how much the poet Blake slipped into his hand, perhaps by sleight of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'innocently' points to Blake's poem Auguries of Innocence: 'Hold Infinity in the palm of your hand'. 'There's no end to' describes that boundless quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Infinity is limitlessness, something with no end, the quantity Blake's line has held in the hand.

clue.text: Panic about heading for Clapham Common? Definitely not

indicators.note: about means the fright word wraps round the next letter

parts.note: a panic is a scare

indicators.note: heading means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Alarm spreads on the way to Clapham Common in south London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' takes C from Clapham and 'about' puts it inside SCARE. Clapham Common is a park in south London; 'Common' is really part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce is in short supply, the opposite of commonplace.

clue.text: No' long delay setting up a few pints?

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting up means the letters are written bottom to top

parts.note: taken as no
a lag is a delay

explanation.surface: No lengthy wait while a few pints are set up at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting up' reverses NO + L + LAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallon is eight pints, so a few pints, with a question mark for the vagueness.

clue.text: Arrange a useful situation at tennis?

definitions.meaning: to set things up is to organise or arrange them
a ... position in tennis is one that leaves a player well placed to win the point, playing also on 'set' as a unit of the match

explanation.surface: A plan for a handy advantage on the tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up is to arrange, and a set-up is a favourable situation contrived in advance.

clue.text: Some bracelets apparently held up as fake

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the letters run bottom to top
some means a run of letters taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: Some bracelets seemingly shown off are imitations.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters ETSAP inside braceLETS APparently, turned round by 'held up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paste is glass used to imitate gems, so paste jewellery is fake.

clue.text: One may make devoted use of such floor covering

definitions.text: One may make devoted use of such floor covering

parts.words: One may make devoted use of such floor covering
parts.note: a rug used devoutly is one knelt on during worship

explanation.surface: A rug that someone uses with great devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devoted' looks like keen enthusiasm but means religious devotion: the rug is knelt on in worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Muslims kneel on a small rug laid on the floor to perform their prayers.

clue.text: A girl I've just met? Mark the song

definitions.text: A girl I've just met? Mark the song

parts.words: A girl I've just met? Mark the song
parts.note: points to the West Side Story number whose lyric runs 'I've just met a girl named' and the name of its title

explanation.surface: Someone tells of a new acquaintance and urges you to note the tune.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue quotes Tony's song from West Side Story, 'I've just met a girl named ...', and 'Mark the song' tells you to take its title.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's title is the girl's name, the heroine of the musical.

clue.text: Machine offering notes to people in the street?

definitions.text: Machine offering notes to people in the street?

parts.words: Machine offering notes to people in the street?
parts.note: suggests a cash machine handing out banknotes to passers-by, but the notes are music heard through headphones by walkers

explanation.surface: A cash dispenser handing out banknotes to passers-by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests banknotes from a cash machine; they are musical notes from a portable player such as a Walkman, listened to while walking.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable cassette or CD player with headphones delivers music to one listener on the move.

clue.text: Recalled little 'correspondence about hour for TV fundraiser

indicators.note: about means the reversed word wraps round the time abbreviation
recalled means called back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: a notelet is a small folded note for brief correspondence

explanation.surface: A short letter was taken back concerning the hour for a charity broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' sends the small letter backwards, and 'about' wraps that round the hour abbreviation, just before its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A telethon is a long televised broadcast appealing for charitable donations.

clue.text: Area of influence to do with charity, mostly

parts.note: re means concerning or to do with

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped from the charity word

parts.note: alms are charitable gifts

explanation.surface: A sphere of activity largely concerned with charitable work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the S from ALMS.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a field or domain, as in the realm of science.
